Symbols are those of the [notation table](methods-overview.html#notation).
R interface: `events` and the comparisons, `Heaviside()` and `sign()` in
the `rhs` of [`cppODE()`](../reference/cppODE.html); `roottol` and
`maxroot` of [`solveODE()`](../reference/solveODE.html).

A *time-triggered event* fires at $t^{*} = t_e(\theta)$, a closed-form
expression. A *root-triggered event* fires where a root function
$h_e(x, t, \theta)$ crosses zero, at $t^{*}(\theta)$ defined by
$h_e(x(t^{*}), t^{*}, \theta) = 0$. Either applies a reset
$$
  x^{+} = R(x^{-}, t),
$$
such as a dose, a clip to non-negative values or a change of regime.

## Restart after an event

Single-step methods (Rosenbrock4, Tsit5) resume at full order. Multistep
methods (BDF/NDF, Adams) restart at order $1$ and rebuild the Nordsieck
array over several steps, the dominant cost under frequent events. Every
method re-estimates the step size from the post-event state with the port
of the CVODES routine `cvHin`
([the first step](methods-stepping.html#the-first-step)), bounded by the
remaining interval; for a single-step method this is the whole restart.

## Sensitivity transport across a discontinuity

The update $S_\theta^{+} = (\partial R/\partial x)\,S_\theta^{-}$
misses the $\theta$-dependence of the firing time. With $f^{-}$ the
right-hand side at $x^{-}$ and $f^{+}$ that at $R(x^{-}, t^{*})$, it
adds two drifts of order $f^{\pm}\,(\partial t^{*}/\partial \theta)$:

1. *Pre-event drift:* $x^{-}$ flows along $f^{-}$ from the grid time
   $t_*^{(0)} := \mathrm{scalar}(t^{*})$ to $t^{*}$, over
   $\delta t^{*} = t^{*} - t_*^{(0)}$, zero in value but not in the
   $\theta$-derivatives.
2. *Post-event drift:* $R(x^{-}, t^{*})$ flows along $f^{+}$ from $t^{*}$
   back to the grid time, over $-\delta t^{*}$.

To first order the two give the [saltation matrix](#saltation). cppDE
applies forward drift, reset and backward drift in dual arithmetic, each
drift one step of Heun's method (explicit trapezoidal rule). The state
receives only the $\theta$-derivatives of the displacement, and the first
and second derivatives of $R$. Without sensitivities, $R$ is a
plain map. $\delta t^{*}$ comes from $t_e(\theta)$ or, for a root, from
the implicit function theorem.

## Time-triggered events

The integrator runs to $t_*^{(0)} := \mathrm{scalar}(t_e)$ and treats
[]{#eq-fixed-dt}
$$
  \delta t^{*} = t_e(\theta) - t_*^{(0)},
  \qquad \mathrm{scalar}(\delta t^{*}) = 0, \tag{1}
$$
as a dual number with tangents $\partial t_e/\partial \theta_a$ and
$\partial^2 t_e/\partial \theta_a \partial \theta_b$. The state $x^{-}$
at $t_*^{(0)}$ has the pre-event sensitivities $S_\theta$ as tangents.
The transport reads
[]{#eq-fixed-heun}
$$
\begin{aligned}
  &\text{forward:}\quad
    f_1 = f(x^{-}, t_*^{(0)}), \quad
    x_E = x^{-} + f_1\,\delta t^{*}, \quad
    f_2 = f(x_E, t^{*}), \\
  &\hphantom{\text{forward:}\quad}
    x^{*} = x^{-} + \tfrac{1}{2}(f_1 + f_2)\,\delta t^{*}, \\
  &\text{reset:}\quad
    x^{*}_{+} = R(x^{*}, t^{*}), \\
  &\text{backward:}\quad
    \tilde f_1 = f(x^{*}_{+}, t^{*}), \quad
    x_B = x^{*}_{+} - \tilde f_1\,\delta t^{*}, \quad
    \tilde f_2 = f(x_B, t_*^{(0)}), \\
  &\hphantom{\text{backward:}\quad}
    x^{+} = x^{*}_{+} - \tfrac{1}{2}(\tilde f_1 + \tilde f_2)\,\delta t^{*}.
\end{aligned} \tag{2}
$$
An Euler step suffices at first order, since the powers
$(\delta t^{*})^{k}$, $k \ge 2$, have no first-order dual content. At
second order the curvature term
$$
  \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(J\,f + \partial f/\partial t\bigr)\,(\delta t^{*})^{2}
$$
remains, because $(\delta t^{*})^{2}$ has the mixed derivative
$$
  \frac{\partial^{2}(\delta t^{*})^{2}}{\partial \theta_a\,\partial \theta_b}
    = 2\, \frac{\partial t_e}{\partial \theta_a}\,
          \frac{\partial t_e}{\partial \theta_b}.
$$
The second Heun evaluation, at shifted state and time $t^{*}$, supplies
it with an error of $O((\delta t^{*})^{3})$. Evaluating
$f_2$ and $\tilde f_1$ at $t_*^{(0)}$ would drop
$\tfrac{1}{2}(\partial f/\partial t)\,(\delta t^{*})^{2}$ for an
explicitly time-dependent right-hand side.

## Root-triggered events

A root event fires at $t^{*}(\theta)$ defined by
[]{#eq-root-condition}
$$
  G(t^{*}(\theta), \theta) :=
    h_e\bigl(x(t^{*}(\theta), \theta), t^{*}(\theta), \theta\bigr) = 0, \tag{3}
$$
in three steps: localization on the scalar trajectory, $\delta t^{*}$ by
the implicit function theorem, transport [(2)](#eq-fixed-heun).

### Localization of the root

$h_e$ is evaluated at the end of every accepted step and at every output
time. A crossing on $[t_n, t_{n+1}]$ is accepted on a sign change or on
$h_e(x_{n+1}, t_{n+1}) = 0$ exactly. A zero at the lower end belongs to
the previous sample, so an event does not fire again on the surface it
was just applied on, where $h_e$ is zero up to round-off.

The crossing is refined on the dense output of the step, without
right-hand-side evaluations, by false position with the interpolation
factor clamped to $[0.1, 0.9]$. The clamp bounds the stagnation of the
classical rule and keeps the speed on a nearly linear $h_e$. It
stops at a bracket narrower than the root tolerance, after
fifty iterations, or at $h_e = 0$. It returns as
$t_*^{(0)} := \mathrm{scalar}(t^{*})$ the end of the final bracket with
the pre-crossing sign of $h_e$.

### Dual residual of the event time

For smooth $G$ with $\partial G/\partial t \neq 0$, the implicit
function theorem applied to [(3)](#eq-root-condition) gives
[]{#eq-dt-star-first}
$$
  \frac{\partial t^{*}}{\partial \theta}
    = -\frac{G_\theta}{G_t}
    = -\frac{\nabla_x h_e \cdot S_\theta + \partial h_e/\partial \theta}
            {\nabla_x h_e \cdot f + \partial h_e/\partial t}\bigg|_{*}, \tag{4}
$$
with the rate $\dot h_e$ at the crossing as denominator. A transversal
crossing has $\dot h_e \neq 0$; at a grazing one $t^{*}$ is not
differentiable in $\theta$ and the fallback of simultaneous events
applies. In dual arithmetic [(4)](#eq-dt-star-first) is the quotient
[]{#eq-dt-star-quotient}
$$
  \delta t^{*} = -\frac{h_e(x^{-}, t_*^{(0)}, \theta)}
                       {\dot h_e(x^{-}, t_*^{(0)}, \theta)}, \tag{5}
$$
on the dual state and parameters at the scalar grid time. The generated
partials $\nabla_x h_e$ and $\partial h_e/\partial t$ serve only
$\dot h_e$; the dual arithmetic forms the numerator. The scalar value of the numerator, of
the order of the root tolerance, is set to zero before the division, so
$\delta t^{*}$ has only derivatives.

At second order the quotient lacks the $G_{tt}$ contribution, since $h_e$
is evaluated at $t_*^{(0)}$, not at the dual time $t^{*}$. Expanding
[(3)](#eq-root-condition) with
$\delta t^{*} = \delta t^{*}_{(1)} + \delta t^{*}_{(2)} + \cdots$ and
$G(t_*^{(0)}, \theta^{(0)}) = 0$ gives
$$
  0 = G_t\,\delta t^{*}_{(2)}
      + \tfrac{1}{2} G_{tt}\,(\delta t^{*}_{(1)})^{2}
      + G_{t\theta}\,\delta t^{*}_{(1)}\,\delta\theta
      + \tfrac{1}{2} G_{\theta\theta}\,\delta\theta^{2},
$$
of which the quotient supplies the $G_{t\theta}$ and $G_{\theta\theta}$
terms. The corrected update, which changes only second-order components,
is
[]{#eq-dt-star-second}
$$
  \delta t^{*} \leftarrow \delta t^{*}
    - \tfrac{1}{2}\,\frac{G_{tt}}{G_t}\,(\delta t^{*})^{2}, \tag{6}
$$
with
$$
  G_{tt} = \frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}}{\mathrm{d} t^{2}}
            h_e\bigl(x(t), t, \theta\bigr)\bigg|_{*}
$$
from generated code, including second time derivatives of forcings.
Where a slide ends, $f$ is continuous and $G_{tt}$ enters scaled by a
zero jump of $f$. The transport [(2)](#eq-fixed-heun) then uses
$t^{*} = t_*^{(0)} + \delta t^{*}$.

### Simultaneous events

Crossings in one step are localized separately; those sharing
$t_*^{(0)}$ within the localization tolerance form a cluster. One forward
shift, every reset of the cluster (the resets are assumed to commute) and
one backward shift cost four right-hand-side evaluations for any number
of events. $\delta t^{*}$ comes from the first event of the cluster with
non-zero $\dot h_e$ and is shared by the others, which sit at the same grid
time with the same parameter dependence through $x^{-}$.

If every event of the cluster has $\dot h_e = 0$, detected by the size
of $|\dot h_e|$, there is no $\partial t^{*}/\partial \theta$ and the
reset is a plain map, exact in
the limit where both $f^{\pm}\,(\partial t^{*}/\partial \theta)$
vanish.

### Conditions switched by a reset

A jump is not a crossing of the continuous solution, so every condition
is evaluated on both sides of a jump:

- a condition whose sign changes across the jump fires there, one per
  sweep, so that a reset can switch on the next condition;
- a condition that held before the jump does not fire again;
- terminal conditions stop the integration instead.

Switched resets are applied between the forward and backward shift of
the causing event. One transport then applies the composition of both
resets, with the sensitivities of a time-triggered event at that time.

## Switches on states and time

$f$ switches where $h_e(x, t, \theta)$, reading a state or the time,
changes sign: in a comparison whose sides differ by $h_e$, and in
$\mathrm{Heaviside}(h_e)$ or $\mathrm{sign}(h_e)$. Read literally, $f$ is discontinuous in $x$: a step
across the switch fails the error test until short enough, and
sensitivities miss the dependence of the switching time on $\theta$.

The code generator keeps each condition as a *mode* $m \in \{0, 1\}$,
$1$ where $h_e > 0$ (or $h_e \ge 0$ for a non-strict comparison);
$a < b$ becomes the mode of $h_e = b - a$. All generated code reads the
mode in place of the comparison, so between switches $f(x, t; m)$ is as
smooth as the branches. $\mathrm{Heaviside}(h_e)$ and $\mathrm{sign}(h_e)$
take two modes, on $h_e$ and $-h_e$, to keep the value at $h_e = 0$.
Equality and inequality stay as written: they switch on a set of
measure zero.

A switch is a root event with condition $h_e$ and the identity as reset.
The crossing step stays on the branch it started on. It is
localized to a few doubles in $t$ rather than to the root tolerance,
since the switching time enters the state through the jump of $f$. The
mode is set between forward and backward shift, so
[(2)](#eq-fixed-heun) uses $f^{-} = f(\,\cdot\,; m^{-})$ and
$f^{+} = f(\,\cdot\,; m^{+})$. To first order this is the
[saltation matrix](#saltation) with $\partial R/\partial x = I$,
$$
  S_\theta^{+} = S_\theta^{-} + (f^{-} - f^{+})\,
    \frac{\partial t^{*}}{\partial \theta},
  \qquad
  \frac{\partial t^{*}}{\partial \theta}
    = -\frac{\nabla_x h_e \cdot S_\theta^{-} + \partial h_e/\partial \theta}
            {\nabla_x h_e \cdot f^{-} + \partial h_e/\partial t},
$$
and second order follows from the same dual arithmetic, with the $G_{tt}$
correction [(6)](#eq-dt-star-second) along $f^{-}$. At a kink the
first-order jump vanishes, and the transport supplies the second-order
term from the jump of $\partial f/\partial x$.

The modes are read off the state at the start of the solve and after
every reset, which can move the state across a switch; after a crossing the mode takes the side the root crossed
to. A switch adds no output row and does not count toward `maxroot`. A state
leaving a root zero at the start of a step, to the side the mode does not
describe, shows no sign change; the departure counts as a crossing once
$|h_e|$ exceeds root residual and rounding.

### Sliding along a switching surface {#sliding}

On the surface a switch takes the side both branches move to, by the
sign of $\dot h_e = \partial h_e/\partial t + \nabla_x h_e \cdot f$
under each mode. For $\dot h_{e,\mathrm{on}} < 0 < \dot h_{e,\mathrm{off}}$
the solution slides [@filippov1988differential] on
$$
  f = a\, f_{\mathrm{on}} + (1 - a)\, f_{\mathrm{off}},
  \qquad
  a = \frac{\dot h_{e,\mathrm{off}}}{\dot h_{e,\mathrm{off}} - \dot h_{e,\mathrm{on}}},
$$
with $\dot h_e = 0$. A slide ends where $a$ reaches $0$ or $1$, another
root, and the solution leaves to that side with continuous $f$. Switches
sliding at once take $\sum_c w_c(a)\, f_c$ over the mode
combinations $c$, with $w_c$ the product of $a_k$ or $1 - a_k$ over the
sliding switches $k$ and $a$ chosen to zero every sliding rate. The solve
stops with an error without such a mix, or when a switch leaves the
surface twice in a row without sliding. The weights are formed in the
scalar type of the model, so the dual sensitivities keep the dependence
on $x$ and $\theta$.

### Switches in the reverse mode and in `cvode()`

The reverse mode stores the modes of each step with the checkpoint, sets
them before the adjoint of the step, and transposes the switch as a root
event ([the adjoint of an event](methods-reverse-events.html#event-adjoint)),
with $f^{-}$ and the derivatives of $f^{-}$ in the old mode and $f^{+}$ in
the new one. While sliding, the weights depend on the state through the
rates $D_k(a) = \sum_c w_c(a)\, \dot h_{k,c}$ held at zero,
$\nabla a = -D_a^{-1} D_x$, and the pullback of $\lambda$ is
$$
  J^{\mathsf T}\lambda = \sum_c w_c\, J_c^{\mathsf T}\lambda
    - \sum_k u_k \sum_c w_c\, \nabla \dot h_{k,c},
  \qquad
  u = D_a^{-\mathsf T} b, \quad b_j = \frac{\partial f}{\partial a_j}\cdot\lambda,
$$
with $\dot h_{k,c}$ the rate of switch $k$ at combination $c$ and
$\nabla \dot h_{k,c}$ the generated gradient of that rate, likewise in
the parameters.

`cvode()` hands $h_e$ to CVODES root finding and at the returned root

- sets the mode,
- adds $(f^{-} - f^{+})\,\partial t^{*}/\partial \theta$ to the
  sensitivities before `CVodeSensReInit()`,
- under adjoint sensitivity analysis starts a new stretch, whose backward
  problem reads the modes of that stretch.

Slides follow the same rule, with two further roots per switch for the
slide ends.

## Saltation matrix {#saltation}

The classical *saltation matrix* adds to $\partial R/\partial x$ a term
for the $\theta$-dependence of the firing time:
$$
  S_\theta^{+} = \frac{\partial R}{\partial x}\,S_\theta^{-}
    + \left( \frac{\partial R}{\partial t}
             + \frac{\partial R}{\partial x}\,f^{-} - f^{+} \right)
       \frac{\partial t^{*}}{\partial \theta}.
$$
The first-order part of the Heun transport equals it, with
$\partial t^{*}/\partial \theta = \partial t_e/\partial \theta$ for
time-triggered events and [(4)](#eq-dt-star-first) for root events; the
transport also gives second order. Implementation: `cppde_saltation.hpp`,
event loop in `cppde_event_engine.hpp`.
